items.objection: The story is based on 015, which is not merged and is 28 commits ahead of main. Every file 016 renames may still change in 015, so the rename can conflict for reasons unrelated to it. The proposal calls this a 'rebase' note for discovery, but it decides whether the story can be delivered as one clean change at all.
items.evidence: proposal: "Base branch is `015-resource-time-buffer`, which is not merged to `main` (28 commits ahead); expect a rebase when 015 changes." and depends_on: ["015-resource-time-buffer"]
items.alternative: State in the story that 016 is delivered only after 015 is merged to main, or that 015 is frozen while 016 is open. Do not treat 'expect a rebase' as an accepted risk. The alternative is to run the rename as the last step after 015 lands.

items.objection: AC-3, AC-4 and AC-5 restate the same rule as AC-1: behaviour is unchanged and only the name differs. They are three more acceptance criteria for one refactor. Each one invites its own test and its own discussion about what 'exactly as before' means.
items.evidence: AC-3: "the instance is created from that schema exactly as before this story"; AC-1: "behaves exactly as the matching /resources/types operation behaved before"; out_of_scope: "Any change of schema or instance behaviour ... other than the name"
items.alternative: Merge AC-1 and AC-3..AC-5 into one criterion: all existing schema and instance operations, including the list filter and the create field, behave as before under the new names. Keep AC-2 (old addresses gone), AC-6 (no 'type' in the API description) and AC-9 as separate criteria.

items.objection: AC-7 covers 'every message' returned by the module that mentions a resource type. The set is not bounded, and it is not shown in any fact whether such messages exist. A criterion that cannot be enumerated cannot be shown complete. The wording gives no way to tell 'done' from 'missed one'.
items.evidence: AC-7: "every message returned to the user by the Resources module that mentions a 'resource type'"; the capability report (F-1..F-4) has no fact about user messages
items.alternative: Have discovery list the concrete messages first, then name them in AC-7 or check them with a text search of the Resources module. Otherwise drop AC-7 and rely on AC-6 plus a search of the source for the old word.

items.objection: AC-1 relies on a 'group owner' with 'the same access rules' as before. F-4 has confidence 'unknown' and says no Resources endpoint is shown as restricted to a role; every endpoint requires only sign-in. The proposal builds its actor and its 'same access rules' claim on a role restriction that the facts do not confirm. The scenarios are then narrower than what is being renamed.
items.evidence: F-4: "Resources endpoints (/resources/types*, /resources/instances*) show no role or group restriction" (confidence: unknown); proposal Actors: "the only role that manages schemas and instances today"
items.alternative: Reword AC-1 and AC-3..AC-5 to 'a signed-in user with the access they have today' unless discovery confirms an owner-only rule. Then the story cannot be read as adding or checking a role rule.

items.objection: The cheapest version that gives most of the value is the API contract, frontend client and messages renamed, plus a table rename. The proposal already rejected the partial options (no database, code only), so I list this only for completeness. Nothing in the proposal shows that a full rename of tables, columns and internal class names is needed for the stated 'why', which is one word in conversation and in the API. The 'why' is met once the public words and the model names match.
items.evidence: why: "one name everywhere before the availability epic builds new code on top of schemas"; rejected_alternatives: "Rename without the database (tables keep the old name)"
items.alternative: Keep the full rename, as decided. Split the work into two deliverables only if 015 keeps moving: first the API and frontend contract, then the internal and database names.
items.addresses_rejected_alternative: Rename without the database (tables keep the old name); Rename only inside the backend code, keep the API and database

items.objection: The discovery notes ask to check internal naming of 'instance' for consistency and report mismatches. This is a second naming audit inside a story whose out_of_scope already excludes renaming 'instance'. It adds discussion for no acceptance criterion.
items.evidence: proposal notes: "check internal naming for consistency and report any mismatch to the owner rather than renaming silently"; out_of_scope: "Renaming 'instance' — the API already uses /resources/instances"
items.alternative: Drop the note, or turn any mismatch found while renaming into a follow-up item outside this story.
